sections.description:
PRESIDENT'S ORDER 22 OF 1985
PRESIDENT'S ORDER
22 OF 1985
HOUSES OF
PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES (ELECTIONS) (TWELFTH AMENDMENT) ORDER,
1985
[Gazette of
Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 19th March, 1985]
No. F. 17 (3)/85-Pub.-The
following Order made by the President is hereby published for general
information :-
In pursuance of the Proclamation
of the fifth day of July, 1977, and in exercise of all powers enabling him in
that behalf, the President is pleased to make the following Order :-
1. Short title and
commencement.--(1) This Order may be called the Houses of Parliament and
Provincial Assemblies (Elections) (Twelfth Amendment) Order, 1985.
(2) It shall come into force at
once.
2. Amendment of Article. 10,
P. (P. P.) O. No. 5 of 1977.--In the Houses of Parliament and Provincial
Assemblies (Elections) Order, 1977 [P. (P. r.) O. No. 5 of 1977], in Article
10, after clause (4), the following new clause shall be added, namely :-
"(5) If a
person elected to the National Assembly or a Provincial Assembly at the
elections held under this Order is found by the Commission to have subscribed,
after the commencement of the Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies
(Elections) (Twelfth Amendment) Order, 1985, either as proposer or seconder, to
the nomination of more than one candidate for a seat or seats, such person
shall cease to be qualified to be a member of such Assembly and his seat shall
become vacant.".
3. Validation.-For the
removal of all doubts, it is hereby declared that, notwithstanding anything
contained in the Constitution or any other law for the time being in force or
the decision of any Court, the nomination of any person for election to the
Senate, held under the Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies
(Elections) Order, 1977 [P. (P. P.) O. No. 5 of 1977] and the Senate (Election)
Act, 1975 (LI of 1975), shall not be deemed to be invalid or defective, and
shall not be called in question in or before any Court, or other authority, on
the ground that the person who signed the nomination of such person either as
proposer or seconder hard not made the oath to be made by a person elected to a
Provincial Assembly.
